questions.question: Two hosts on different IPv4 subnets in different VLANs must communicate. Their switch only forwards at Layer 2 and has no uplink to a router. What is required?

options.A: Connect both hosts to access ports in their current VLANs.
options.B: Provide inter-VLAN routing via a router or Layer 3 switch.
options.C: Disable VLAN tagging on every switch port.
options.D: Configure the same MAC address on both hosts.

questions.explanation: A Layer 3 gateway must route between the two subnets. VLAN separation is not removed by configuring access ports.

option_explanations.A: Access ports retain membership in separate VLANs and do not route between their subnets.
option_explanations.B: A Layer 3 gateway must route between the two subnets. VLAN separation is not removed by configuring access ports.
option_explanations.C: Removing tags does not create a Layer 3 gateway or merge the IP subnets.
option_explanations.D: Duplicate MAC addresses can disrupt switch learning and do not provide routing.
